text:
sarah: Quick check — I'm about to land a Terraform tweak for embeddings-worker: change replica_count 3 -> 5 and switch the k8s object to a StatefulSet rolling update with partition behavior so we can phase the upgrade. Also renaming a mounted secret path from /etc/old-secrets to /etc/worker-secrets. Any red flags?

mike: Why StatefulSet? embeddings-worker is mostly stateless, right? If it's truly stateless a Deployment with maxSurge/maxUnavailable gives smoother rolling updates.

sarah: It's not completely stateless — local LM cache and PVC-backed kvstore per replica. We need ordinal stability. Hence StatefulSet.

nina: For StatefulSet rolling updates, partition is the way to do phased upgrades. Remember RollingUpdate.strategy.partition controls which ordinals are updated; there's no maxUnavailable for sts. Plan: set partition to current highest ordinal to update one pod at a time. :+1:

ashley: Also check readinessProbe timing — if we scale from 3->5 the new pods can thrash on resource limits. Suggest bumping cpu/mem for init phase or add startupProbe to avoid premature failure.

ops-bot: terraform plan check: detected secret path rename in k8s manifest. CI note — make sure secret sync PR runs before apply or mounts will 404 in new pods.

sarah: Good call. I'll split into two PRs: (A) secret rename + kustomize overlay + secret-sync job, (B) replica bump + sts updateStrategy change.

mike: For PVCs: if you're using volumeClaimTemplates the controller will create PVCs for new ordinals automatically, but they need underlying storage class capacity. If using static PVCs make sure TF creates the additional PVCs or the pod will stuck Pending.

nina: If we want a safer canary, consider updating partition to 2 (so ordinals 0..1 remain on old), then incrementally lower partition to roll. That gives manual control.

ashley: FYI our HPA is tied to cpu/memory metrics on a Deployment -> for StatefulSet metricsServer scaling works but we don't have an HPA for this service currently. If we plan to scale dynamically later, keep that in mind.

sarah: snippet of what I'm planning to push in the k8s manifest (FYI):
```yaml
updateStrategy:
  type: RollingUpdate
  rollingUpdate:
    partition: 4  # start with only ordinal 4 on new image, then lower to 3,2...
```
and terraform var: `replica_count = 5`

mike: Small nit: partition is the ordinal index to keep at old revision. If you have 5 replicas and set partition:4, only pod 4 will be left on old (or new?) double-check logic in K8s docs — it's easy to invert.

ashley: Correct: partition N means ordinals >= N get updated? I always look it up each time too. Let's test in dev cluster.

ops-bot: I added a pre-apply GH check to detect missing PVCs for target replica_count and a secret-mapping diff check. CI job: infra/validate-pvc-secret.

sarah: Thanks — I'll hold the PR until we've run the validate job and a dev cluster canary. Planning: PR A this afternoon (secrets), PR B tomorrow (replicas + strategy).

deploy-bot: Reminder: when you do the canary, tag the image with `canary-<pr>` and set partition=4 then watch readiness and logs for 15m before lowering partition.

nina: I'll volunteer to watch canary for the first 30m. Ping me when PR B is ready.

sarah: Awesome. will ping here with the dev canary link. thanks everyone :rocket:
